verdicts.title: The committed uv.lock still resolves accelerate 1.14.0, which carries an open GitHub-reviewed advisory with a released fix
verdicts.reasoning: Independently reproduced. /home/user/opaque/uv.lock:40-56 pins accelerate 1.14.0. I re-ran an OSV querybatch over all registry-sourced packages in uv.lock myself (217 entries, not 218) and got exactly one hit: accelerate 1.14.0 -> GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 / PYSEC-2026-3804 / CVE-2026-69112, MODERATE, github_reviewed_at 2026-09-08, CWE-22, ranges {introduced 0, last_affected 1.14.0}. OSV returns {} for accelerate 1.15.0, and PyPI confirms 1.15.0 exists (uploaded 2026-09-09), so a fixed version is available. uv.lock:2862 / :4146 confirm accelerate is pulled transitively by peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0. .github/dependabot.yml:47-66 is as described (uv ecosystem, versioning-strategy lockfile-only, groups: workspace-dependencies patterns ["*"], weekly Monday). So the factual core of the finding holds. BUT the framing and the stated impact are both wrong, which is why I dropped severity two notches: (1) 'a fix exists and was simply not taken' is not supportable - uv.lock was last modified 2026-09-07 (git log -1 -- uv.lock), the fixed 1.15.0 was published 2026-09-09, and the Dependabot uv lane fires Mondays, i.e. 2026-09-14, the day after this snapshot; no fixed version existed when the lock was last written. (2) The exploit path is not reachable from anything this repo ships or runs: accelerate is not a declared dependency of any published opaque wheel (only transitive through peft/trl, which are dev-group and extras), transformers 5.16.1 in the lock does not even depend on accelerate, and grep over the whole tree finds zero uses of load_checkpoint_in_model / load_checkpoint_and_dispatch / dispatch_model. The only device_map= in the repo is packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_training.py:539. The finding's claim that 'exactly what examples/train_*.py do' triggers this is false - none of the eight examples/ scripts uses device_map or a sharded-index loader. The advisory itself is AV:L/UI:R: it needs an operator to point an accelerate checkpoint loader at an attacker-controlled shard index. Net effect today is dependency-scanner noise in dev/CI environments plus a one-line lock bump.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The committed uv.lock pins accelerate 1.14.0, the last version affected by GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 (path traversal / DoS via unsanitised weight_map entries in load_checkpoint_in_model and load_checkpoint_and_dispatch). Every `uv sync --group dev --all-packages --extra all` and every CI lane therefore installs a package with a live MODERATE advisory, and any repo-wide OSV/pip-audit scan will flag it. The fixed 1.15.0 was published 2026-09-09, two days after uv.lock was last regenerated (2026-09-07), and the weekly Dependabot uv lane had not yet run, so this is a pending bump rather than an ignored fix. No Opaque code path is exploitable: accelerate is only a transitive dependency of peft/trl (dev group + extras, not a dependency of any published opaque wheel), the repo never calls load_checkpoint_in_model / load_checkpoint_and_dispatch / dispatch_model, and none of examples/train_*.py passes device_map. Remediation is `uv lock --upgrade-package accelerate`; the durable value in the finding is its secondary suggestion - the grouped `workspace-dependencies` Dependabot lane means a security bump rides with unrelated updates, and there is no OSV/pip-audit check over uv.lock or Cargo.lock in CI (I confirmed zero OSV hits across Cargo.lock's crates as well).

verdicts.title: third_party_provenance.toml misattributes riskcal to a nonexistent google-research repository, and one upstream's homepage is prose rather than a URL
verdicts.reasoning: Both defects exist in the current tree, though at different line numbers than cited (drift: riskcal homepage is /home/user/opaque/third_party_provenance.toml:105, not 126; the random-allocation homepage is :82, not 112). (1) riskcal: the file declares homepage = "https://github.com/google-research/riskcal". WebFetch of that URL returns HTTP 404. The real project is https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal (MIT, 'Measure and calibrate operational privacy risks for differentially private algorithms'), and PyPI riskcal 1.5.1 metadata gives project_urls = {'Repository': 'https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal.git'} with license MIT; a web search corroborates authorship by Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez under the interpretable-dp org, not Google Research. So the manifest credits the wrong organization and points at a dead URL. (2) The 'Random-allocation reference implementation' entry does put a prose sentence in the homepage field, verified verbatim at :82. Severity dropped from medium to low on impact, not on fact: the riskcal entry is disposition = "inspired", requires_notice = false, and riskcal appears nowhere in NOTICE (I grepped), so no published wheel or NOTICE currently misstates attribution - the error is confined to an internal inventory file. The random-allocation entry's NOTICE text (NOTICE:107-118) already identifies the upstream only by paper title and Apache-2.0 terms, the same granularity as the toml, so the toml is not degrading an existing published attribution. ARC-009 is marked Planned in .junie/architecture-contracts.md and the manifest-to-NOTICE generator does not exist yet; there is also no schema or validator anywhere in the repo that defines `homepage` as a URL (grep for third_party_provenance finds no consumers), so 'homepage must be absolute http(s)' is the auditor's reasonable convention rather than a stated contract. The riskcal wrong-URL half is a genuine one-line factual fix worth making on a public repo; the prose-homepage half is a data-quality nit.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: third_party_provenance.toml:105 attributes riskcal to https://github.com/google-research/riskcal, which does not exist (HTTP 404); the real upstream is https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal (MIT, by Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez), so a checked-in provenance file on a public repository credits the wrong organization and gives an unresolvable link. Separately, third_party_provenance.toml:82 stores a sentence ('ICML 2026 reference implementation for "Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation"') in the homepage field, so that upstream has no resolvable reference at all even though it is disposition = "adapted" with requires_notice = true. Impact today is limited to this file: riskcal has requires_notice = false and appears nowhere in NOTICE, and NOTICE's random-allocation section (NOTICE:107-118) already identifies that upstream by paper title only, so no published wheel or NOTICE text is currently wrong. The exposure is that ARC-009's planned NOTICE generator would propagate both values the moment it is built, and that anyone doing an attribution review from this file cannot reach either upstream.

verdicts.title: The repository's squash setting discards every PR body, contradicting AGENTS.md and the PR template and disabling git-cliff's BREAKING CHANGE detection
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end, including the repository setting. GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque (authenticated) returns squash_merge_commit_title = "PR_TITLE", squash_merge_commit_message = "BLANK", allow_merge_commit = false, allow_rebase_merge = false; the main ruleset further restricts allowed_merge_methods to ["squash"]. AGENTS.md:64-66 says the opposite ('the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`). Both feed `git-cliff`'), and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 repeats it ('On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads'). I proved the behaviour rather than inferring it: PR #974 (Dependabot) has a multi-kilobyte body, was squash-merged on 2026-09-07, and the resulting commit 9eabd4c6 has a completely empty body - Dependabot always writes a body, so this is conclusive. Every one of the 40 most recent commits under 12146ec4 has an empty body or only Co-authored-by trailers. cliff.toml:40 does contain { body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE", group = "Breaking" } and cliff.toml:44 sets protect_breaking_commits = true, so that parser can never fire. Two corrections that pull severity down to low. First, the finding overstates the documentation spread: CONTRIBUTING.md:255-260 is actually consistent with the real setting ('the PR title is the commit message on `main`') and documents only `!` for breaking changes, so the contradiction is confined to AGENTS.md:64-66 and the PR template, not to CONTRIBUTING.md. Second, cliff.toml's sibling parser { message = ".*!:", group = "Breaking" } still works, and the team uses `!` in titles in practice (b9b0a23e fix(transformers)!:, 873de427 delete(dpsgd)!:, e8f87cd1 fix(dpsgd)!:, f2d90d61 fix(random)!:, 79acf31d fix(accounting)!:), so no release has actually lost a Breaking section - the hazard is latent, triggered only by a contributor who follows AGENTS.md's footer option instead of `!`. No code, artifact, or privacy impact; the real cost is the permanent loss of PR rationale from git log.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The repository is configured squash_merge_commit_title = PR_TITLE, squash_merge_commit_message = BLANK (verified via the authenticated repo API), so every squash commit body is empty apart from GitHub's Co-authored-by trailers - demonstrated by Dependabot PR #974, whose long body produced an empty body on commit 9eabd4c6. AGENTS.md:64-66 and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 both tell contributors the opposite (CONTRIBUTING.md:255-260 is correct and only documents `!`). Two consequences. (a) The 'why' prose the PR template asks for never reaches git log or release notes. (b) cliff.toml:40's { body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE" } parser and protect_breaking_commits = true read the commit body and can therefore never fire, so a contributor who follows AGENTS.md:78 and declares a breaking change with only a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the PR body gets the commit grouped by its type prefix instead of under Breaking in the drafted release notes. This has not yet happened: every breaking commit in the delta range uses `!` in the title, which cliff.toml's message parser still catches. Fix is either setting squash_merge_commit_message = PR_BODY or deleting the footer option from AGENTS.md and the body parser from cliff.toml.

verdicts.title: The required status check "Qodana / Qodana" can never report on a fork pull request, so the documented external-contribution path cannot merge
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified, including the one the finding itself only rated 'medium' confidence. Ruleset: GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/rulesets/12831618 (enforcement active, ~DEFAULT_BRANCH) requires exactly seven contexts, one of which is {"context": "Qodana / Qodana", "integration_id": 15368}; the pull_request rule requires 1 approving review and allowed_merge_methods ["squash"]; bypass_actors = [{RepositoryRole 5, always}]. Workflow: .github/workflows/pr.yml:248-272 - job `qodana`, `name: Qodana`, guarded by `if: (success() || failure()) && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, calling ./.github/workflows/qodana.yml whose jobs.scan is `name: Qodana` (qodana.yml:28-31), giving the composed context 'Qodana / Qodana'. I then proved the skip behaviour empirically instead of assuming it: in run 34686188621 (draft PR #1030, sha c4be0b93, the other branch of the same guard) the jobs API reports a single job named exactly 'Qodana' with conclusion 'skipped', and the check-runs API for c4be0b93 lists 'Qodana' skipped with no 'Qodana / Qodana' entry at all, while 'Python tests' and 'Rust tests' both report success. So when the guard is false the required context is never created, which is precisely what would happen for a non-draft fork PR, and a required context that never reports leaves the PR at 'Expected - waiting for status to be reported'. The contrast the finding draws is also real: pr.yml:186-217 ('Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules', with jq that tolerates skipped python-tests-cuda* legs) and pr.yml:231-247 (rust-test-gate) apply exactly the gate pattern that Qodana lacks. docs/development/index.md:3,9-11 and README.md:185-186 do document the fork path, and allow_forking is true. Severity cut from medium to low on impact: forks_count is 0, so no fork PR has ever been opened; the sole merger of record (evgri243, merged_by on #974) holds the admin role that the ruleset grants bypass_mode 'always'; and the guard itself is defensible because .github/workflows/ci.yml:167 shows Qodana needs secrets.QODANA_TOKEN, which GitHub withholds from fork pull_request runs, so running it unguarded on forks would fail rather than help. The residual defect is genuine but narrow: a first external contributor sees a permanently pending required check and needs an admin to bypass, and fork PRs get no static-analysis coverage.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The active main ruleset (id 12831618) requires the context 'Qodana / Qodana', which is produced only when pr.yml's `qodana` caller job instantiates the reusable qodana.yml `scan` job. That caller is guarded by `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` (and `!draft`), and I verified on the draft branch of the same guard (run 34686188621, sha c4be0b93, PR #1030) that a skipped caller emits a check run named 'Qodana' with conclusion skipped and no 'Qodana / Qodana' check run at all. A non-draft pull request opened from a fork - the path docs/development/index.md:3,9-11 and README.md:186 tell external contributors to use, with allow_forking true - therefore has one of its seven required contexts permanently unreported ('Expected - waiting for status to be reported') and cannot be merged except by a user holding the admin role the ruleset grants bypass_mode 'always'. It also receives no Qodana coverage, though that part is partly unavoidable since ci.yml:167 shows Qodana needs secrets.QODANA_TOKEN, which fork pull_request runs do not get. No fork has actually hit this yet (forks_count = 0) and the repo's regular merger is an admin who can bypass, so the practical cost is a blocked or confusing first external PR. The fix is the gate-job pattern already used at pr.yml:186-217 ('Python tests') and pr.yml:231-247 ('Rust tests'): add an `if: always()` job named e.g. 'Qodana gate' that passes on success or skipped, and require that context instead.
